subject: Markets dip, Bitcoin steadies near $80k as SpaceX secures $40bn AI‑chip financing

S&P 500 down 0.5%, crypto eyes Fed, SpaceX taps $40bn debt, Nigeria Ebola‑free, Saudi logistics resilient.
Armonia Capital
The Morning Balance · Monday, 26 October 2026

Today's balance

U.S. equities slipped, with the S&P 500 at 7,623.68 (-0.52%) and the Nasdaq at 25,955.34 (-0.21%). Commodities showed mixed signals; gold rose 0.71% to 4,036.2 while the dollar edged higher to 101.871. The most significant driver today is the convergence of central‑bank policy decisions and their impact on risk assets, particularly crypto and AI‑related financing.

Market snapshot

SPX 7,623.68 USD ▼ 0.52%IXIC 25,955.34 USD ▼ 0.21%XAU 4,036.20 USD ▲ 0.71%DXY 101.87 USD ▲ 0.06%BTC 80,282.00 ▼ 0.08%ETH 2,324.24 ▼ 0.24%

Prices at the time of writing; may be delayed.

Top stories

Bitcoin holds near $80,000 as oil retreats and the Fed decision looms
The price steadied amid expectations of upcoming Federal Reserve rate guidance, highlighting crypto’s sensitivity to monetary policy. Source →

SpaceX enters $40 billion deal with Apollo for AI chip financing
SpaceX is raising $40 bn of investment‑grade debt to purchase Nvidia GPUs, a move that could reshape AI‑hardware funding and set a benchmark for high‑yield tech debt. Source →

Nigeria has no Ebola cases after patient evacuation – WHO
WHO confirmed Nigeria is Ebola‑free following the evacuation of an infected patient, removing a public‑health risk and supporting economic recovery. Source →

Saudi imports hold up despite Houthi shipping attacks
Saudi Arabia’s import volumes remained stable despite ongoing maritime disruptions, underscoring the resilience of its supply chains. Source →

Bahri places $450 million order for very large oil tankers
The state‑owned shipping group placed a $450 million order for VLCCs, signaling continued investment in fleet capacity and competitiveness in the Gulf. Source →

Today's analysis

SpaceX’s $40 B AI‑Chip Debt Deal Shifts the AI‑Hardware Equilibrium

SpaceX’s $40 billion off‑balance‑sheet debt raise to fund Nvidia GPUs may redraw the balance between AI‑hardware supply, corporate financing costs and equity valuations.

Read the full analysis →

Regional watch

Europe. Euronews reports Galp and Moeve failed to agree a merger of refining and distribution operations, a setback for consolidation in the Iberian energy sector. Source →

Africa. Nigeria’s stamp‑tax proposal threatens manufacturer margins and consumer spending, raising concerns for domestic industrial output. Source →

Asia. India extends duty‑free cotton imports through December, supporting textile manufacturers amid global supply‑chain pressures. Source →

MENA. Morocco plans a social‑media ban for users under 15, a policy shift that could affect digital entrepreneurship and youth engagement in the region. Source →

What to watch today

  • Federal Reserve rate decision expected Wednesday; crypto and equity volatility may react sharply.
  • SpaceX debt terms to be finalised by the syndicate; interest rate and maturity will influence AI‑related credit spreads.
  • Saudi Ministry of Transport funding increase of 15% announced in September 2025 may affect freight rates and logistics sector performance.

Featured asset of the day

ASML (ADR) (ASML, stock)
ASML designs and manufactures extreme‑ultraviolet (EUV) and High‑NA lithography systems that print the microscopic circuit patterns on silicon wafers; its customers are the world’s leading semiconductor makers such as Intel, TSMC and Samsung.

In focus today. The recent $40 billion AI‑chip financing deal announced by SpaceX underscores accelerating demand for advanced chips, which in turn drives immediate need for ASML’s next‑generation lithography tools.

Risks: Tight export‑control regimes that could restrict sales to key customers. The extremely high cost of High‑NA systems may delay orders if semiconductor manufacturers curb capex amid macro‑economic uncertainty.

Editorial spotlight for its real-world utility. Not a recommendation to buy or sell.
